Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.

Welcome
Welcome to Bruton Primary School, where we are focused on raising achievement by working together.
Welcome to our website, we hope it will give you an insight into our school. Our school is in Bruton, a small historic town situated in the Brue Valley in South Somerset.
All of our staff and governors work hard to make our school one that is safe and nurturing as well as stimulating and exciting for our children. Our new curriculum encompasses the demands of the Curriculum 2014 which is enhanced and developed to match the needs of our children through a range of Quests – we believe that all children have the potential to become confident and independent learners. We try to support them to strive for this and start them on a journey of exploration that will last them a lifetime. This enquiry based learning is supported by the development of Personal, Learning and Thinking skills (PLTs) which are skills believed to prepare our children for the world in which we send them.
We are fortunate to have amazing school grounds – our classrooms frame the brightly painted playground we call the quad and there is also an amazing school field and top playground where there is a range of wooden play equipment and a new bespoke trim trail. We have a developed forest school area with a pond, which was opened by the Lord-Lieutenant of Somerset and many outside learning areas within our large school site. We are also very lucky at Bruton Primary School to have our very own swimming pool which we use as much as we can in the Summer Term.
The Reception classes have been developed and established so that it embraces child initiated learning both inside and outside. The outside area has been updated and enhanced and is a truly inspiring place for our youngest children to explore and learn together.
At Bruton Primary School we raise achievement by working together. We want our children to develop a sense of self-worth and to become positive and successful learners and future members of society. Our Quests encourage them to focus on local, national and global enquiry and we link as much as we can with the local community involving our parents in their children’s learning by inviting them into school to celebrate, share and discover together. We try to create a joint endeavour – a shared journey – with the same thing firmly at the core of that journey – our children.
Bruton Primary School is a happy, vibrant school full of happy, vibrant children and adults – We are very proud to be the Executive Headteacher and Head of School here and would welcome the opportunity to show you around and share what makes us great with you.
Please feel free to contact the school and arrange a visit. We look forward to meeting you.
Mrs Rachael Bisset and Miss Sapphire Giles
Executive Headteacher & Head of School

Maths
Mathematics statement of Intent
At the East Somerset Federation, the teaching of mathematics aims to ensure that children are fluent in the fundamentals of the subject; are able to reason, both verbally and in writing; and are also able to solve problems in a range of contexts across the curriculum and in everyday life.
At the East Somerset Federation, we aim for every child to:
We follow the objectives as outlined in the national curriculum but use the White Rose Schemes of Learning to support our implementation of these objectives. We place considerable value on children having a secure understanding of the fundamentals of the subject and therefore use the Number Sense factual fluency programme to support this in KS1.
Following a mastery approach as endorsed by the DfE and the NCETM, our lessons use a range of practical resources and visual representations to support children's understanding of mathematical concepts. Children are routinely given opportunities to practise and consolidate on previously learned concepts as this is vital to move this knowledge into their long term memory.
We have 5 maths lessons per week in all classes, with each lesson 60 minutes long. In addition to this, children will regularly access 10 Tough Ten Maths arithmetic questions upon arriving to school. KS1 pupils will receive a 10 minute daily Mastering Number session. In years 3 and 4 children will continue to develop their factual fluency with our schools times tables approach. Furthermore, children regularly practise their times tables at home using TT Rockstars and we have 3 whole school competitions annually with an end of term awards assembly.

Science
We want our children at East Somerset Federation to acquire knowledge, skills, concepts and positive attitudes whilst deepening their understanding across all scientific disciplines. We will use the National Curriculum to support teaching and learning and will provide opportunities for whole school investigations enabling children to apply skills and knowledge.
Working scientifically will be embedded and children will develop an intrinsic desire to question the way the world around them works. They will develop the necessary skills to investigate and apply this knowledge beyond the scientific classroom.
Children will build upon prior knowledge as they progress through the school and will be eager to share their learning using scientific terminology and vocabulary.

Community Kids Breakfast & After School Club
Bruton Primary School works very closely with Community Kids who provide a Breakfast and After School Club for Bruton Primary School children. Community Kids escort the children to and from school at the beginning and end of the day.
Breakfast club is open from 8am until 8.45am Monday to Friday. For Primary School age children the cost is £4.20 per hour.
After School club runs from 3.30pm until 6.00pm, Monday to Friday. For Primary School age children the cost is £4.20 per hour.
For further information and to book a place, please contact Community Kids on 01749 813933 / 07596 766869 or visit www.communitykidsbruton.co.uk.

Bruton Primary Art Gallery
Kingfisher created some collagraph prints, inspired by our work on Greek architecture!
Cuckoo Class have been looking at the artist Paul Klee. We created our own portraits, copying his style, using oil pastels and watercolours.
At Hauser and Wirth Years Three and Four continued with the project - joining up with other children from our Federation. They experimented with texture, movement, surface and colour as the language of emotion.

Kingfisher produced some Harvest art based on the work of Dennis Wojtkiewicz.
Year 3/4 visit to Hauser and Wirth
Reception and Year One had an inspiring trip to Hauser and Wirth to see the work of the sculptor Phylldia Barlow. They created their own sculptures, made some collaborative sculptures and used them to create their own sculpture gardens.
Royal Academy Young Artists' Competition - after the children had created their work to submit to the exhibition, the parents were invited to see the art. It was lovely to have them in the classroom celebrating what their children have achieved.
Year 5 made them own stamps out of plasticine and then used these to print their own Mayan logograms.
Ibis class have used different methods of printing to create their piece of art to enter into our art competition.
Ibis Class have looked into different artists who use collage as their media. We then chose a theme linking to the rainforest and created our own collage and mixed media pieces of work.
Year Three and Four made self-portraits in the style of Roy Lichtenstein.

Welcome to our Computing page
Our Federation Computing Mission Statement
An excellent Computing education enable pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has strong links with mathematics, science and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, where pupils are taught the ideas of information and computation, how systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming.
Building on this, pupils are able to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world.
We use Teach Computing to deliver a range of exciting and motivating Computing lessons which challenge and inspire the children and we use ActiveBytes to deliver lessons to educate and encourage children to be Safer Online Citizens.
This is the overview of Computing in our school. The order of units may change to fit with what we are teaching in Quest.
